prompt: An arithmetic sequence starts at $a_1 = 5$ and adds $d = 4$ each step. Find $a_{10}$.
hint: Use $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$. The first term has taken ZERO jumps, not one.

hints.text: Use $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$. The first term has taken ZERO jumps, not one.
To reach term $10$ you take $10 - 1 = 9$ jumps of size $4$, which is $36$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the jumps on your fingers
steps: Term 1 is 5 with no jumps yet. Term 2 is 9 after one jump. Term 3 is 13 after two jumps.
Notice the pattern: the jump count is always one less than the term number.

alternativeExplanations.title: List it out to check
steps: Count the numbers you wrote: exactly ten of them.
The tenth is 41 — the formula and the list agree, and the list is a great safety net for small n.
